notes: Article is a furniture-led DTC brand; its only in-scope decor is Lighting and Mirrors, so the row list is legitimately short. Site reached DIRECTLY over IPv4 (HTTP 200) - article.com is A-only with no AAAA, but egress worked this run, so no translate.goog proxy was needed. Storefront is a Vue/Nuxt SSR app; every /browse/ listing server-renders its own exact total as an 'N items' string in the Sort & Filter header, which is what every qty below comes from. Full decor tree taken from /category_sitemap.xml plus the live sidebar on /browse/48/decor: Decor (370 items) has live children Mirrors 19, Lighting 88, Rugs 132, Pillows 59, Bedding 27, Poufs 11 - only Mirrors and Lighting are in scope (rugs/pillows/bedding are textiles, poufs are seating). Three former decor children are dead: /browse/26/decor-accents and /browse/77/decor-throws both 301 to the Decor parent, and /browse/80/decor-care-products 301s to a single touch-up-kit product, so there is no accents/objects/vases category to extract. Verified by site search that Article has no wall art, vase, clock, tray or candle-holder category - those queries return fuzzy whole-catalogue matches (e.g. 'wall art' -> 1848 items, larger than the entire decor tree), not category pages. Sanity checks passed: the four Lighting children sum to 86 against a parent of 88 (2 items carry no sub-type), and the six live Decor children sum to 336 against a parent of 370 (the ~34 gap is ex-Throws stock that no longer has its own category page). Counts vary correctly per URL, so none is a site-wide total. Lighting parent (88 items) is emitted as a grouping row with null qty per the contract. Item counts are product-family counts; individual colour variants have their own /product/ URLs and are more numerous.
